coverageNotes: Tests the implicit creation-time suffix. No claim about equal-timestamp tie direction, custom timestamps, pagination, or production throughput.

questions.concept: Implicit creation-time suffix on an ordinary index
questions.context:
Using Convex 1.44.0, comments has fields postId: string, author: string, text: string and .index("by_post", ["postId"]). Three comments for postId="p" have distinct creation times: text "Beta" is oldest, "Zulu" is next, and "Alpha" is newest. Comments for other posts also exist. A query validates { postId: string } and runs:

```ts
return await ctx.db.query("comments")
  .withIndex("by_post", (q) => q.eq("postId", args.postId))
  .order("desc")
  .collect();
```
questions.question: For { postId: "p" }, what happens?

options.text: It returns the comments in text order: "Zulu", "Beta", "Alpha".
options.rationale: text is not an index field and does not determine this query order; the seeded text order differs from creation order.

options.text: It returns the comments newest first: "Alpha", "Zulu", "Beta".
options.rationale: Ordinary indexes have an implicit _creationTime suffix. With postId fixed, order("desc") traverses that suffix newest first.

options.text: It returns the comments oldest first: "Beta", "Zulu", "Alpha".
options.rationale: An ascending-order control returns this sequence; the displayed query explicitly reverses that order.

options.text: It throws because by_post does not explicitly include _creationTime.
options.rationale: The unchanged by_post index supports the displayed query. Explicitly declaring _creationTime is unnecessary.
